title: Student Life, Clubs, Library and Digital Services
text:
Studying at International Burch University (IBU) is not only about attending lectures and passing exams. The university offers students clubs, cultural events, hands-on projects and a number of digital services that make studying easier.

Students from more than 25 countries study at IBU, so the student community is multicultural. According to the Explore page, students can join more than 30 clubs, societies and events. Through the clubs, students get mentorship and professional opportunities.

The student clubs page lists SpeakUp Club, Business Development Club, Diplomacy Club, Burch Economica, GBE Student Collective, Arch Team, Civil Designers, ACM, High Voltage Club, DEN Club, International Students Club, Illustration Club, SAP, IBU Adventures, Sport Club and FVP Club. The names show that some clubs are linked to a field of study, such as architecture, civil engineering, electrical engineering, economics or diplomacy, while others are about sports, illustration, outdoor trips or bringing international students together.

Student Club Day 2026 was held on 21 October 2026. At this event, students met the clubs that are active at the university, learned what they do and found out how to join. For many students it was their first contact with the clubs. According to the university, clubs help students build confidence, organizational and communication skills and make friends across departments and years of study.

The library is another important part of student life. Since October 2026, the IBU library has been a full member of the COBISS.BH library and information system, which connects it more closely with libraries in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the region. Through cooperation with the National and University Library of Bosnia and Herzegovina, students and academic staff have gained access to additional library collections, reading rooms, academic databases and interlibrary loan services.

On the Student Area page, students find quick links to the systems they need during their studies. These are the Student Information System (SIS), the Learning Management System (LMS), student e-mail and the library. Microsoft Office 365 is free for all active student and staff e-mail accounts of the university. IBU also has a campus-wide MATLAB license, so students can use MATLAB and Simulink without limits on and off campus, on any device. The university also uses EPRINTS, an open-source digital repository. The same page also links to the academic calendar and to information about the Erasmus+ program.
